summary.intent: Diagnose and fix three interrelated issues with `mise run test`: garbled/interleaved output making failures hard to read, a hidden test failure, and slow/hung test runs (both unit and integration).
summary.outcome: Five concrete bugs were fixed (timezone-sensitive test, ANSI escape leak from huh form, non-deterministic TUI dismissal, integration test inheriting real TTY, integration subprocess hitting real OS keyring), `mise run test` was switched to `gotestsum --format pkgname` and `test:integration` to `gotestsum --format testname`, and all changes were committed to branch `codex/local-testing-improvements`.

repo: `groupCommitsByDay` groups by `t.Local()` calendar day, making any test with UTC-boundary fixtures fail in non-UTC timezones (Melbourne collapses two January dates into one local day)

The integration test suite is a single Go package (`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test`), so `go test` and `gotestsum --format pkgname` both print nothing until all ~324 tests complete — making it look frozen
`TestMain` in the integration suite builds a real `entire` binary before any tests run, adding a one-time compile cost

`RunEnableWithAccessibleMode` used plain `exec.Command` (not `execx.NonInteractive`), causing the child `entire enable` subprocess to inherit the real `/dev/tty` and block waiting for interactive agent-selection input
`TestLogin_SavesTokenAfterApproval` ran a real `entire login` subprocess with no keyring isolation, hitting the machine keyring and failing with `exit status 161`
`gotestsum` is already installed in the project but was unused; the `huh` form library defaults to writing directly to the terminal unless explicitly given `WithOutput`
The slowest unit tests are `runExplainCheckpoint(generate=true)` variants in `explain_test.go` — they exercise real summary provider resolution rather than a cheap stub

code.finding: `groupCommitsByDay` uses `t.Local().Format(...)` — correct production behavior but makes tests timezone-sensitive
Fixture timestamps were UTC RFC3339 strings that crossed a local day boundary in AEST; fixed by building them as noon in `time.Local`
`huh.NewForm` was not given `WithOutput(w)`, so the colored `Repository name` prompt leaked to the real terminal even though the function accepted a writer
TUI sink tests didn't send a dismiss keypress after `RunFinished`, causing them to block when stdin wasn't wired by the test runner
`RunEnableWithAccessibleMode` used `exec.Command(...).CombinedOutput()` — child inherited real TTY and hung waiting for interactive input
`TestEnableDefaultStrategy` is the test that timed out after 10m because it called the above helper
Added `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE` env var to redirect auth token storage to a temp file in subprocess tests, bypassing the OS keyring
Login integration test ran `entire login` subprocess with no keyring isolation; wired to set `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE` pointing to the test env's temp dir
`test` task changed to `gotestsum --format pkgname --format-icons text --format-hide-empty-pkg`; `test:integration` changed to `gotestsum --format testname --format-icons text --hide-summary skipped`

workflow: `go test -json | jq 'select(.Action=="output" and ((.Output|contains("\r")) or (.Output|contains("\u001b"))))...'` is the right pipeline for finding ANSI/control-char leaks from specific tests
Testing timezone stability with both `TZ=UTC` and a high-offset zone like `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` catches both under-UTC and over-UTC day-boundary collapse
`gotestsum --format testname` is the correct format for single-package test suites; `pkgname` produces no intermediate output for them
`gotestsum tool slowest --jsonfile <events.json> --threshold 5s` produces a ranked list of slow tests from a captured run
Reproducing a TTY-sensitive hang requires running the test from an actual PTY session, not a subprocess without a terminal

friction: Initial `gotestsum` switch appeared to deadlock `cmd/entire/cli/review` — turned out to be an artifact of interrupting a long run mid-flight, not a real incompatibility; caused wasted investigation and a premature revert
`test:integration` looked completely frozen under raw `go test` because all 324 tests are in one package with no intermediate output — visually indistinguishable from a real hang
The `huh` form `WithOutput` API is easy to miss; nothing in the function signature or linter flags that the form is writing to a default writer instead of the passed-in one
The OS keyring failure (`exit status 161`) only surfaces in full uncached integration runs, not in the targeted single-test invocation, making it easy to miss during incremental verification
`cmd/entire/cli` package takes ~60s because `go test ./...` doesn't stop on first failure and slow summarizer/explain tests run unconditionally
open_items: `test:ci` task was left on raw `go test` — not switched to `gotestsum` because the CI environment wasn't validated

The slow `runExplainCheckpoint(generate=true)` tests in `explain_test.go` (~10-15s each) were identified as the dominant cost in the unit suite but not addressed — they exercise real summary provider resolution
Unrelated uncommitted changes in `.opencode/package-lock.json` and `docs/file-edit-tool-hooks.md` were excluded from the PR and remain on the worktree
Whether other integration tests besides login hit real system resources (keyring, network, credentials) was not fully audited — the keyring fix was targeted at the one known failure
